reason: 2.1.1 means to give a list nested in another list a top margin of a quarter of --femto-typography-spacing-vertical and no other margin, in :where(dl, ol, ul) :where(dl, ol, ul). That selector has zero specificity, so the earlier dl, ol, ul rule wins: a nested ul, ol or dl keeps margin-top 0 and the full typography spacing as margin-bottom, and the next item sits 16 to 20px below the nested list instead of the 4 to 5px gap between list items (0 after a nested dl, whose items have no margins). 1.x wrote the second half as :is(dl, ol, ul), and 2.0 changed it to :where(). femto writes :where(dl, ol, ul) :is(dl, ol, ul). Its specificity is (0,0,1) and it comes after the list rule, so nested lists get the quarter-spacing top margin and no bottom margin. Like 1.x's rule, it matches any list inside a list, not only a direct child of li or dd: a list in a card, blockquote, accordion or .grid within a list item also gets margin 0 and the quarter top margin, and in loose items (li > p) the gap after a nested list becomes the item gap (4 to 5px) while the gaps around the paragraphs keep the full spacing. Rules with higher specificity still win: the dropdown menu keeps its margins, and lists inside nav keep margin-bottom 0, so a list nested in a nav list gains only the top margin.
notes: Fixtures: content-typography.html (ul > li > ul, ul > li > ol, ol > li > ol, dl > dd > dl and dl > dd > ul) and kitchen-sink.html (ul > li > ul, ol > li > ol and dl > dd > ul). Their margin-top goes from 0 to 4px at 390 and 5px at 1280, and their margin-bottom from 16px and 20px to 0, in Chrome Beta 158 and Firefox 160 beta, ltr and rtl, in every scheme. Probed with standalone Selenium pages in Chrome 158 and Firefox 160 beta at 500, 800 and 1280px (roots of 16, 18 and 20px), ltr and rtl, light media and data-theme=dark, with the same numbers in both browsers: at 800 the gap from a nested ul or ol, or a ul in a div in an item, to the next item goes from 18 to 4.5px, the plain item gap, and a parent item's text to its nested list from 27 to 31.5px; a nested dl to a following ul in the same dd from 18 to 4.5px; a list nested in an aside list from 31.5 to 18px above the next item; in an aside nav (aside > nav > ul > li > ul) the nested list gains a 4.5px top margin and the gap after it stays 9px. In a loose item (li > p, then a nested ul) the gap from the nested list to the next item's paragraph goes from 18 to 4.5px, while the paragraph to nested list step stays 18px, as in 1.x. Unchanged: top-level list margins, the plain item gap, the gap from the last nested item to a following paragraph, dropdown menus in and outside a nav (summary to menu 2.25px) and the docs-style aside (nav > details > ul). A computed-style diff of every tests/pages page at 500 and 1000px, ltr and rtl, changes nothing but these lists, the heights of their containers (nested-list-margins-container-size) and, below them, absolutely positioned elements (nested-list-margins-breadcrumb-shift). The nav case has no harness fixture. Upstream issue picocss/pico#672; upstream commit 00f1486a changed 1.x's :is() to :where().

reason: Consequence of nested-list-margins: a nested list trades 2.1.1's full bottom margin for the smaller quarter-spacing top margin, so the li or dd that holds it, the outer list and every ancestor up to the document get shorter by the difference, and their transform and perspective origins follow.

reason: 2.1.1 declares --femto-font-size: 0.875em on small, but no rule applies it: only html, :host and h1 to h6 set font-size: var(--femto-font-size). So small keeps the browser's font-size: smaller, the parent size divided by 1.2 (0.8333em: 13.33px under 16px text, 14.17px under 17px). Pico 1.5.13 had small { font-size: var(--font-size) }; 2.0.0 kept the token and lost that rule. femto applies the token in content/typography.css, so small is 0.875em of its parent (14px under 16px text, 14.875px under 17px), 5% larger than in 2.1.1, and its line-height and the em-based sizes of its descendants, such as a code element, grow with it. A small nested in another small or inside a heading compounds as it did with smaller, and the hgroup subtitle rule (1rem) still wins. An author rule that sets small's font-size and loads before femto, or sits in a cascade layer while femto is unlayered, now loses to femto's rule, where it used to beat the browser's smaller; setting --femto-font-size on small now takes effect.
notes: Fixtures: every small of the pages listed in small-font-size-container-size: inline in paragraphs (content-typography.html, kitchen-sink.html, tokens-base.html and its shadow root, tokens-schemes.html and its shadow roots), helper text after inputs, selects, valid and invalid fields and a .grid (forms-basics.html, including its data-theme islands, kitchen-sink.html, classes-grid.html, the forms-input-* pages and tokens-schemes.html), small in a figcaption (content-figure.html), small holding code (content-code.html) and the nav helper of components-nav.html. In Chrome Beta 158 and Firefox 160 beta, in every leg and direction, small goes from 13.3333px to 14px at 390 (16px root) and from 16.6667px to 17.5px at 1280 (20px root), its line-height from 20px to 21px and from 25px to 26.25px, a block helper from 19.98px (Firefox 20px) to 21px tall at 390 and from 25px to 26.25px at 1280, and code inside small from 11.6667px to 12.25px at 390. Probed with standalone Selenium pages in Chrome Beta 158 and Firefox 160 beta at 375, 600 and 1300px, light and dark, ltr and rtl, at rest, with a link hovered and an input focused, against 2.1.1, femto before the fix and the built dist. Before, every small was 0.8333 of its parent with both 2.1.1 and femto (14.1667px under 17px text); after, 0.875 (14.875px; Firefox reports 14.8833px, rounded to 1/60px) in a paragraph, an rtl paragraph, h2 (24.79px to 26.03px at 600) and h6, a nested small (11.81px to 13.02px under 17px text), a link, a button, a figcaption, a blockquote footer, li, td, a card footer, data-theme light and dark islands, a small with its own data-theme and a shadow root. code and sub inside small keep 0.875em and 0.75em of it, and the hgroup subtitle small stays 1rem. No color, background, border, margin, padding or display changed anywhere. Upstream pull request picocss/pico#561 adds the same declaration; upstream commit 8b4f1527 (set root font size to 100%) removed 1.x's small rule and kept the token.

reason: Consequence of small-font-size-token-applied: a block small, such as helper text under a form field, is taller with its larger font size and line-height, and a small holding code can raise its line, so the elements that contain it, up to the document, get taller, and their transform and perspective origins follow. The entry is limited to the pages that hold a small.
